newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 12.

text.p: FINANCIAL TIMES
STERLING SURGES TO 52-MONTH HIGH AGAINST D-MARK

The latest sharp rise in the value of sterling has once more prompted a number of British companies to warn of the likely impact on their profit margins. The increase is also likely to strengthen the hand of chancellor Kenneth Clarke in his resistance to Bank of England pressure to a rise in UK interest rates. However, the deputy governor of the bank has warned that even the beneficial effects of sterling's rise will not result in the government reaching its stated inflation target.
UNILEVER SEEKS 6 BILLION STG FROM SPECIALITY CHEMICALS SALE

Unilever has announced that it is planning to divest itself of its speciality chemicals unit, raising in the region of between 5 and 6 billion stg in the process. The company will make use of funds raised to strengthen its position in the areas of personal products and food. The announcement came as something of a surprise to the market, though was well received, with Unilever shares rising in both London and Amsterdam.
ITC CALLS FOR SINGLE TV REGULATOR

Speaking to a committee of MPs, Sir Robin Biggam, the chairman of the Independent Television Commission, has called for the setting up of a single UK TV regulatory body. He noted that the present situation, which sees responsibility divided between various parties is both confusing and costly. The director- general of the BBC, John Birt, has expressed criticism of the idea, however, observing that it would create a new monolith.
REUTERS SAYS STRENGTH OF STERLING MAY HIT TRADING

Financial information and media group Reuters has reported an increase of 17 per cent in pre-tax profits for 1996 to 701 million stg. The company was, however, cautious about the outlook given the current strength of sterling and the effects of the introduction of new products. 85 per cent of the group's revenues are derived from outside the UK, making it particularly vulnerable to currency movements. Peter Job, Reuters chief executive, revealed that the company is continuing to examine options for the return of some of its 1.05 billion stg cashpile to investors following the abandonment of a previous share buyback plan.
TORIES TO CONTINUE WITH SELL-OFFS

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke has given a commitment that the Conservative government will continue on its programme of disposals of public assets. He noted that Labour opposition to such a strategy made it the "enemy of enterprise". He cited a report compiled by the Conservative think tank, the Centre for Policy Studies, which has concluded that privatisation has resulted in lower prices and better services for consumers.
CONSUMERS "SPEND MORE ON SMALL INDULGENCES'

Market research company Mintel in its annual report on lifestyles in Britain has concluded that increasingly consumers are spending their money on small indulgences such as ready meals, magazines and visits to the cinema. At the same time people are exhibiting a marked reluctance to invest their money in large purchases such as holidays. The report also highlights the large increase that has taken place in spending on financial services over the past decade.
MINISTER UPBEAT ON ELECTRICITY TIMETABLE

Speaking before a Commons energy committee, government minister Lord Fraser has expressed confidence that the electricity sector will be ready for the advent of competition by April of 1998, a deadline set down by the industry's regulator. He noted that plans were being prepared for the possibility of companies missing the deadline, noting, however, that such contingencies would be costly for the companies involved. This mood of optimism is not, however, matched by senior executives within the electricity sector itself.
AMSTRAD CUTS DEFICIT DESPITE RESTRUCTURING

The UK computer and telecoms company Amstrad has announced a reduction in its losses for the first half to 1.78 million stg. The company also revealed that it was setting to one side a further 6.4 million stg to cover the costs of the restructuring of its consumer electronics unit. Had it not been for this charge Amstrad would have reported profits of 1.91 million stg for the period.
COACH GROUP AWARDED FIFTH RAIL FRANCHISE

The coach group National Express has been provisionally awarded the franchise to operate Central Trains rail services in the Midlands, Anglia and north Wales. This marks the fifth such franchise to be awarded to the company, placing it ahead of Prism Rail which operates four services. Meanwhile, a seven-year franchise to operate the Thameslink rail service has gone to the GoVia consortium, a pairing of the Go-Ahead group and Via GTI of France.
BANKERS FIGHT PLAN TO GIVE CUSTOMS EXTRA POWERS

The British Bankers' Association has added its voice to criticism being expressed of a provision of the Finance Bill that proposes extending the powers of Customs & Excise to seize unpaid tax. Under the plans Customs & Excise would be allowed to approach banks directly to secure payment of such liabilities directly from the assets of those concerned. Although a similar system operates in Scotland already, critics point out that the new arrangements for the rest of the country do not include a judicial process.
